issue_context.title: optimize query cluster_slow_query when there are many slow-log files.
issue_context.body:
## Description

[TiDB Dashboard slow query page](https://docs.pingcap.com/zh/tidb/stable/dashboard-slow-query) will use the below query to query slow queries:

```sql
SELECT * FROM `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`.`CLUSTER_SLOW_QUERY`
    WHERE (time between '2020-09-24 15:23:41.421396' and '2020-09-25 17:57:35.047111') 
    ORDER BY Time desc
    LIMIT 10;
``` 

When there are too many slow-log between `2020-09-24 15:23:41.421396` and `2020-09-25 17:57:35.047111`, such as 10G slow-log files, the upper query execution will be very slow. 

The propose of this issue is want to speed up the query execution time.

### Optimization Hint 1

The current query plan is:

```sql
explain SELECT * FROM `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`.`CLUSTER_SLOW_QUERY`  WHERE (time between '2020-09-24 15:23:41.421396' and '2020-09-25 17:57:35.047111') ORDER BY Time desc LIMIT 10;
+--------------------------+----------+-----------+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| id                       | estRows  | task      | access object            | operator info                                                                                                                                          |
+--------------------------+----------+-----------+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| TopN_8                   | 10.00    | root      |                          | information_schema.cluster_slow_query.time:desc, offset:0, count:10                                                                                    |
| └─TableReader_17         | 10.00    | root      |                          | data:TopN_16                                                                                                                                           |
|   └─TopN_16              | 10.00    | cop[tidb] |                          | information_schema.cluster_slow_query.time:desc, offset:0, count:10                                                                                    |
|     └─Selection_15       | 250.00   | cop[tidb] |                          | ge(information_schema.cluster_slow_query.time, 2020-09-24 15:23:41.421396), le(information_schema.cluster_slow_query.time, 2020-09-25 17:57:35.047111) |
|       └─TableFullScan_14 | 10000.00 | cop[tidb] | table:CLUSTER_SLOW_QUERY | keep order:false, stats:pseudo                                                                                                                         |
+--------------------------+----------+-----------+--------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

As you can see, there is a TopN executor since the SQL query has `ORDER BY Time`. But, the slow log file is already ordered by time, just like an index, so that it is unnecessary.

*You can get 1500 points after implementing this optimization.*

### Optimization Hint 2

As you can see from the query, it retrieves *latest N* slow logs. However, the underlying implementation to scan slow log only supports scanning in ascending order. It means the single slow log file must be fully scanned in order to retrieve the last N records from it. This logic can be improved as well.

*You can get 1500 points after implementing this optimization.*

How about adding some test for multiple time range? Such as:

```sql
(time > '2020-02-16 18:00:00' and time < '2020-05-14 20:00:00') or 
(time > '2020-02-17 18:00:00' and time < '2020-05-17 20:00:00') or 
(time = '2020-02-16 18:00:00')
```
No, in this case, `PKIsHandle` should be false.
